utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Case number IT-01-42-PT, the Prosecutor versus Miodrag Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. First of all, Mr. Jokic, can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may be seated, Mr. Jokic. May I have the appearances from the Prosecution and the Defence. First the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you and good afternoon, Your Honours. Susan L. Somers, Senior Trial Attorney. To my immediate left is Philip Weiner, trial attorney; to my far right, Susan Grogan, case manager; to my right, Ms. Susan Lamb from our legal advisory section; and behind me, Mr. Dean Manning, investigative section team leader.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Somers. For the Defence, could I have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, Ms. Somers and the team. My name is Zarko Nikolic and in this case I will be the chief counsel for Mr. Jokic, and together with me is Mr. Eugene O'Sullivan as co-counsel and Jelena Nikolic, the legal advisor in the Defence team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nikolic. This hearing takes place as a consequence of a joint motion filed by Prosecution and Defence to schedule a hearing to accept accused Miodrag Jokic's change of plea and entry of plea of guilty to a second amended indictment. This hearing has been scheduled orally although there was -- initially there was a hearing scheduled for yesterday. Yesterday, for technical reasons, only a 65 ter meeting was held, and because there was not sufficient time, this hearing was scheduled orally. I take it that the parties have found no prejudice by this scheduling on very short notice. If that would be -- if there would be any prejudice, I'd like to hear from the parties. So being there no prejudice, as far as this hearing is concerned, whenever there is any subject the parties would like to deal with in closed or private session - I think private session would usually do - please ask me so that the Chamber can consider whether we turn into private session. The order I would like to follow is that we first discuss briefly the plea agreement entered by the parties, especially the commitments the parties made, and after that, since we all are aware that if the plea agreement -- that the Chamber has some -- has had some access to a -- to this -- of course to this plea agreement but also access to an amended indictment that would be needed -- an amendment to the indictment that would be needed to be approved, or at least leave granted to amend the indictment in accordance with the text. So therefore, after we went through the plea agreement, I would like to give an opportunity to the Prosecution to apply for leave to amend the indictment, then hear the plea of the accused on the amended indictment, and then we'll see whether we can proceed right away in giving a decision whether or not to accept the plea and to enter a finding of guilt or whether we have to postpone and continue at a later date. So first of all, I would like to speak about the plea agreement that has been submitted to the Chamber. It says that the Prosecution intends to file a second amended indictment and that the accused intends to enter a plea of guilty to that second amended indictment. I would say that's the very basic part of the plea agreement as it's set out in the motion. The reduction of the indictment mainly is that the charges will be limited to the shelling of the old city of Dubrovnik on the 6th of December, 1991, and that the accused will be charged with six counts: Murder; cruel treatment; unlawful attack on civilians; devastation not justified by military necessity; unlawful attack upon civilian objects; and destruction or wilful damage done to institutions dedicated to religion, charity, and education, the arts and sciences, historic monuments, and works of art and science. The factual basis of the new indictment -- the factual basis of the agreement is mainly that the charges are reduced to specifically displace at this moment, although the shelling of the city -- of the old town of Dubrovnik on the 6th of December, 1991, still was part of an armed conflict that was going on already for a longer period of time. There are a few other issues as well in the plea agreement. I would like to refer to the parties that, apart from these basic elements, we have other issues such as the waiver of rights of you, Mr. Jokic. You're not entitled to call any witnesses any more if there is no trial. Therefore, there are a lot of other technicalities which we find in the subsequent paragraphs of the plea agreement. Does any of the parties ask for any detailed discussion of the technical part of the plea agreement?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The Prosecution does not if the Chamber is satisfied with what is before it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence also doesn't feel the need to discuss any of the issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course I did not mention one of the issues that might be of vital importance for you, Mr. Jokic, is that the parties also agreed that the Prosecution would ask for a sentence to be imposed on the basis of a new indictment of ten years of imprisonment, and one of the rights you kept, Mr. Jokic, that if you want to argue at the sentencing hearing that your sentence should be below ten years of imprisonment, you're fully entitled to do so. I would like to ask whether any of the other Judges have any questions in respect of the plea agreement as it has been --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge El Mahdi would like to have a -- to put an additional question or observation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may, I'd like to ask the Prosecution whether it is well understood by the parties that Mr. Jokic could have pleaded -- since he could plead guilty, but nevertheless he could still bring forth some mitigating evidence in order to reduce his responsibility. Do the parties understand that?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is understood that there will be a sentencing hearing at which submissions by both parties will be presented to the Chamber and all factors that would be relevant for the Chamber's consideration, including, of course, mitigating factors, will be included.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, but I'd like to be quite sure that both parties -- and I simply wanted to make sure that both parties understood that fully. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Mr. Jokic, are you aware of the fact that the agreement, the plea agreement you entered into, specifically as far as the sentence to be imposed if your new plea would be accepted does not bind the Chamber, so that it's not a guarantee that if the Prosecution asks for not more than ten years of imprisonment, that the Chamber is still free to impose the sentence as it deems appropriate?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm fully aware of that fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I also take it that you have discussed in full detail with counsel the plea agreement and that you have studied, together with counsel, the new indictment as it will be submitted, I expect soon, by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I therefore conclude that you were under no pressure by whomever, under no coercion by whomever to enter into this plea agreement and that you feel no pressure or no coercion by anyone if you're invited later this afternoon to enter into a plea on a new second amended indictment once leave has been granted to the Prosecution to amend the indictment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no coercion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Jokic. The next step to be taken in order to proceed on the basis of the plea agreement is that the amended -- the indictment should be amended. In other cases sometimes pleas have been entered on part of the indictment and then only later the remaining parts were stricken by an amendment. That is not possible in this case I would say, so, Ms. Somers, if you would like to make an oral application to amend the indictment, this is the time to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The Prosecution in fact does make the application pursuant to Rule 62 ter and Rule 50 to amend the existing amended indictment and is prepared to submit in open court, if it would be of assistance, the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think the proper procedure would be that you deliver a copy of the indictment as it would stand after amendment to the usher, that Madam Registrar would take care that it will be filed right away at the Registry, and we could then proceed after we have taken a decision on the -- on your application for leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: We are prepared to do that right now, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it, Ms. Somers, that this is an exact copy of the second amended indictment as it has been distributed before, but then, of course, there was a draft and it was not -- if the Defence would like to have a look at the submitted amended indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Usher, would you, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is that, and this is an identical copy to the draft.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber now would like to check whether it's also identical with the copies they received, so if it could be given to the Bench for a second. Yes. Ms. Somers, I do understand that there are two annexes to the indictment, but one is missing. Oh, they are coming.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. They're on the way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar. I take it, Ms. Somers, that although the Rules are not quite clear on joinder and severance of cases, that this includes the severance of this case from the case of the co-accused Strugar and Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is not great uniformity in practice, and what the Prosecution is doing is filing a second amended indictment as to the accused Strugar and Kovacevic will be filed this afternoon. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I'm just taking that the Rules are not quite clear on that because severance prior to the trial -- as a -- at the beginning, sometimes the Rules suggest that you need leave for that as well, but that is, I take it, part of this whole procedure, that the cases against Mr. Jokic and co-accused are severed and that a new amended indictment will be filed against the co-accused.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Jokic, you'll certainly understand that this application is made by the Prosecution on the basis of the plea agreement, so it might be common understanding for all of us that if a guilty plea would not follow, that of course the Prosecution would reinstall either the old indictment or ask for further amendments, and it's -- the Chamber, under these circumstances, might well grant such -- such an application. If I would summarise the new --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm clear on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Just to summarise the new indictment, if leave is granted, would be that there are six charges remaining, the first three being murder, cruel treatment, and attacks on civilians, all being the result of the shelling of the old town of Dubrovnik on the 6th of December, 1991. The forces involved and the structures are mentioned in Annex 1 to this second amended indictment. More factual, this shelling caused, according to the second amended indictment, the death of two civilians, Pave Urban and Tonci Skocko, and the wounding of three other civilians, Mato Valjalo, Ivo Vlasica, and Nikola Jovic. This shelling - and these are the three remaining counts of the second amended indictment - also amounted to the devastation of a number -- of which six are specified, of a number of buildings not justified by military necessity. It amounted to unlawful attacks on civilian objects and destruction or wilful damage to institutions dedicated to religion, charity, and education, the arts and sciences, historic works, and works of art and science. Annex 2 to the amended indictment lists, in 51 pages, the destruction and the damage done to those objects and buildings. Before we proceed, we first have to take a decision on the leave to be granted to amend the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber grants leave to amend the indictment. That means that from now on, we are proceeding on the basis of the second amended indictment. Mr. Jokic, the Chamber invites you to enter pleas on each of the counts of the second amended indictment. Madam Registrar, do you have the -- no. Then I will read them myself. Judge El Mahdi just reminded me that if -- that I perhaps first should ask you whether you want to have the charges read in full detail or whether I could limit myself to the counts of the indictment, that means count 1 up to 6, Mr. Jokic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't think that I should have the charges read in full. I have studied the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Jokic, on count 1, murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Common Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949 and punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal, how do you plead on count 1?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the Trial Chamber records the plea of guilty on count 1, murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war. Mr. Jokic, count 2: Cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Common Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber then records the plea of guilty on count 2 of the second amended indictment. Mr. Jokic, on count 3: Attacks on civilians, a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Article 51 of Additional Protocol I and Article 13 of Additional Protocol II of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber records the plea of guilty on count 3 of the second amended indictment. Mr. Jokic, on count 4: Devastation not justified by military necessity, a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Articles 3(b) and 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber records the plea of guilty on count 4 of the second amended indictment. Mr. Jokic, on count 5: Unlawful attacks on civilian objects, a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Article 52 of Additional Protocol I to the Geneva Conventions of 1949, and customary law, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber records the plea of guilty on count 5 of the second amended indictment. We now come to the final count, Mr. Jokic, count 6: Destruction or wilful damage done to institutions dedicated to religion, charity, and education, the arts and sciences, historic monuments and works of art and science, a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Articles 3(d) and 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber records the plea of guilty on count 6 of the second amended indictment. Mr. Jokic, please be seated. The Chamber has to satisfy itself, Mr. Jokic, that the guilty plea you've just entered -- you may remain seated -- that this guilty plea has been made voluntarily, that there were no threats, no coercion, that this plea was informed, that this plea is not equivocal, and that there is a sufficient factual basis for the crime and for your participation therein. I think we already discussed the -- that you entered of your own free will into the plea agreement, and the guilty plea being one of the consequences of this agreement, I take it that you made that plea -- those pleas on six counts, that you made them voluntarily as well. I also take it that because of the assistance you received from counsel, that your plea was informed. And since we discussed yesterday at a 65 ter meeting some details of the understanding of the then still draft second amended indictment, I take it that all the parties agree on what the indictment exactly says and that, therefore, the guilty plea was not equivocal in whatever way. The last issue we have to consider is whether there is a sufficient factual basis for the crime and the participation of the accused therein. The Rules of Procedure and Evidence give us some clue as to how to establish such a factual basis. There are two alternative ways, although they do not exclude each other, to establish the sufficient factual basis for the plea. The first one is independent indicia on the guilt or the lack of any material disagreement between the parties about the facts of the case. Am I right in establishing that the parties do not materially disagree on the facts of the case, the case being now limited to the charges contained in the second amended indictment?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: There is agreement, Your Honour, as to the facts which underlie the specific provisions of the amended indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that is true as far as the Defence is concerned as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is, Your Honour. I can just confirm what Ms. Somers has just said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber nevertheless would like to hear whether there would also be independent indicia that would support the guilty plea. It should not be done in detail, but if a short explanation could be given what independent indicia would support the guilty plea, the Chamber would like to hear it now. Ms. Somers, could you address the Chamber in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: May I be clear that I understand what Your Honour is asking. Are you asking if the Prosecution is prepared to put on a full case involving testimony or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. It's just -- it's just to give a brief indication. For example, if the accused has pled guilty to devastation of buildings, that an independent indicia to support such a guilty plea would be, for example, that there is evidence by photographs or whatever way. You don't have to go into too much detail but there is evidence which support that these buildings were destroyed and that there is evidence that such events took place on that specific day. You don't have to go into very much detail but just in order to satisfy the Chamber that it's not just the plea -- the agreement between the parties but that there is also evidence, I would say material evidence, that would support the guilty plea.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, for the clarification. The Prosecution would indicate that there are witnesses and documents as to all the allegations in the indictment that would support findings independent of the admission of guilt of the accused. The Prosecution submits that, in total, these documents would amount to proof beyond and to the exclusion of every reasonable doubt as to the culpability of the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the basis of the disclosed documents and the disclosed statements of potential witnesses, would the Defence agree that there is also independent evidence apart from the admission of the accused that would support his guilty plea?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. We have -- before we signed the agreement, we went through these documents, and we established that there was relevant material which corroborated the Prosecution's allegations, and the agreement was signed only after that. But I should like to seize this opportunity to say that had the indictment been in this form from the beginning, this wouldn't have lasted so long. Mr. Jokic would have pleaded the same way he did today had it been worded like this in the first instance. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, what would have happened if things would have been different, that's, well, perhaps not at this moment something we should pay a lot of attention to but rather look forward than look back. The Chamber will briefly adjourn in order to consider and to deliberate whether we can proceed at this very moment or whether we should Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. postpone a decision on the acceptance of the guilty plea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, before we proceed, the Trial Chamber would like to turn to private session only for a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, the Chamber accepts your plea and will now pronounce its findings on your guilt. Mr. Jokic, this Trial Chamber finds you guilty on count 1 of the second amendment indictment, murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war. This Chamber, Mr. Jokic, finds you guilty on count 2 of the second amended indictment, cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war. This Trial Chamber finds you guilty on count 3 of the second amended indictment, attacks on civilians, a violation of the laws or customs of war. Mr. Jokic, this Trial Chamber finds you guilty on count 4 of the second amended indictment, devastation not justified by military necessity, a violation of the laws or customs of war. This Trial Chamber finds you guilty on count 5 of the second amended indictment, unlawful attacks on civilian objects, a violation of the laws or customs of war. And it finds you guilty on count 6 of the second amended indictment, destruction or wilful damage done to the institutions dedicated to religion, charity, and education, the arts and sciences, historic monuments and works of art and science, a violation of the laws or customs of war. And this finding of guilt relates on all six counts, both to the responsibility under Article 7(1), and Article 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Please be seated. Madam Registrar, the Registry is instructed to set a date for a sentencing hearing but is invited first to consult the Chamber before finally setting such a date, and I would like to hear from the parties at this moment whether they have any specific time frame in their minds as far as the scheduling for the filing of pre-sentencing briefs or a sentencing hearing is concerned. May I first give an opportunity to the Defence or has this been discussed among the parties?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it has been discussed among the parties. We would respectfully ask for closed or private session for the following discussion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will then turn to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The next issue on our agenda is the motion that has been filed by the Defence for provisional release for the continuation -- or the reinstalling the provisional release of the accused. I am informed that for reasons of privacy, that the Defence would like to say a few words about it in private session. Is that correct, Mr. Nikolic? I see nodding yes. I take it that's -- then we turn to private session again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session again. The Chamber will consider the application for provisional release. It will not give a decision today. The Chamber, however, commits itself to giving a decision on short notice, presumably not later than next Friday. Is there anything at this moment one of the parties would like to raise, or you, Mr. Jokic, would like to raise at this very moment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have nothing to raise at this moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And from the silence of the parties, I conclude that neither the Prosecution nor the Defence wanted to raise any other issue. We'll then adjourn.

procedural_notes.text: ---  Whereupon the Plea Hearing adjourned at
